purpose: Concept review only. No game assets changed.
userRuling: The darker concepts are closer but too dark. Even neutral key lighting on ships works and should prevent strong locale tint.

prompts.prompt: Use case: lighting-weather. Make a single targeted revision to this 16:9 game concept paint-over. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the darker revised version. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL overbright game screenshot, provided ONLY as the upper brightness limit. The user says Image 1 is closer but too dark, and specifically approves its EVEN NEUTRAL KEY LIGHTING ON THE SHIP. That ship lighting is the crucial invariant. Preserve Image 1's ship identity, exact small size, pose, position, neutral ivory and red hull colors, even illumination, and bright-readable silhouette. The ship should have consistent soft neutral-white key and balanced fill, unaffected by the locale color. Do not add colored washes to its hull or make its illumination dramatic, shadowy, brighter or darker. Preserve the HUD layout and text, all objects, composition and stylized painterly/cel-shaded art language. Change ONLY the background value balance: lift the dark and middle tones enough to recover satisfying color and cloud/surface detail across the scene. Aim about one-third of the way from Image 1 toward Image 2 in background brightness, with a more generous range of colored midtones. Keep local highlights and bloom as restrained as Image 1; do not return the cream/white overexposure of Image 2. The result should feel colorful and alive, with readable depth even on an ordinary monitor, while the neutrally lit ship remains the visual anchor. Do not simply lift blacks into a flat gray haze. Retain true deep shadows in pockets, soft highlight rolloff and saturated colored midtones. This is a brightness refinement, not a new composition, not new UI, and not new objects. Output only the single edited game view, no labels or comparison layout. Reveal more of the existing coral/russet cloud folds and muted amber-orange illumination across the warm background. Retain the quiet warm region behind the ship. The clouds should feel warmly luminous in places without becoming a wall of orange light; avoid a nearly black blood-red-only palette.
